summary: 7 Wonders is a fast-playing card drafting game where each player builds up a small civilization over three ages, picking one card from a hand and passing the rest along, simultaneously with everyone else. It plays quickly even at high player counts because interaction is mostly limited to your two neighbors, via military conflict and resource trading, while your own tableau engine runs mostly in parallel.
praised: fast simultaneous play that scales well to large groups
variable wonders and strategies keep it replayable
criticised: scoring can feel like a disconnected point salad with little narrative arc
military and science can snowball and feel a bit swingy
limited direct interaction beyond your two neighbors
some find the endgame scoring math fiddly and anticlimactic

interaction.kind: card drafting with neighbor-only conflict and trading
interaction.detail: Players draft cards from a shared, rotating hand and can only fight or trade resources with the two players seated beside them, so most of the tableau you build is your own private board while the drafted card pool is the only shared state.

scoring.why: final score is a sum of several unrelated categories (military, coins, wonders, civilian buildings, science, guilds) with little overlap between them
scoring.how_you_win: you win by accumulating the highest total score across these disparate categories, often by picking one or two engines (like science or military) to specialize in while staying safe elsewhere
